descs.t: Representative Thomas Massie of Kentucky says he will force a House vote to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth when Congress returns next week, unless Hegseth resigns, CNN reports. Massie calls the war with the Islamic Republic illegal, and some Republican lawmakers are privately blaming Hegseth for the midterm losses. This video walks through the plan, the votes it needs and what happens next.

After the party's historic midterm losses, Thomas Massie is moving to impeach Pete Hegseth over the war with the Islamic Republic, and CNN reports some Republicans expect it could pass. This video looks at why the blame is landing on Hegseth, what an impeachment vote in the House would and would not do, and what it says about where the GOP is heading on foreign policy.

Thomas Massie wants Pete Hegseth impeached for the war with the Islamic Republic, and some Republicans shaken by the midterms may go along. This video makes the case that the vote puts American pressure on the regime itself on trial, and asks what the Islamic Republic and its militias learn if Washington punishes the man who confronted them.

intro.plain: Thomas Massie says he will force a House vote to impeach Pete Hegseth when Congress returns next week, unless Hegseth resigns. That is per CNN. Massie calls the war with the Islamic Republic illegal, and some Republicans are privately blaming Hegseth for the midterm losses. Chat, does this vote pass?
intro.mid: The midterms went badly for Republicans, and now one of their own wants the Defense Secretary gone. Thomas Massie plans to force an impeachment vote on Pete Hegseth next week over the war with the Islamic Republic, and CNN reports some Republicans think it could pass. Chat, is this about the war or about the election?
intro.bold: Thomas Massie wants to impeach Pete Hegseth for taking the fight to the Islamic Republic. After the midterms, some Republicans may join him. If Washington punishes the man who confronted the regime, the regime notices. Chat, would you vote yes or no on this, and why?

hook.plain: Thomas Massie says Pete Hegseth resigns or faces an impeachment vote next week. Here is what Massie wants, who might join him, and what a House vote would do.

hook.bold: A Republican congressman wants to impeach the Defense Secretary for confronting the Islamic Republic. Here is why that vote matters far beyond Washington.

descs.t: Texas has flipped blue in the 2026 midterms, and Elon Musk had bet big on keeping it red. Democrats won the US Senate seat, the governor's race and the Texas House, and Ted Cruz says he is now the only statewide elected Republican, while reports say Republicans kept their Texas Senate supermajority. This video walks through what flipped, what Republicans still hold, and what it could mean for Musk's business empire.

Elon Musk bet big on a red Texas and lost, as James Talarico flipped the Texas Senate seat and Democrats took the governor's office and the Texas House. CNN, the Los Angeles Times and Newsweek are asking what happens to his business empire now. This video looks at the stakes for Musk, the reported Republican move to strip the new lieutenant governor of power, and the fraud claims already spreading online.

A Texas Republican called it a political extinction: Democrats flipped the Senate seat, the governor's race and the Texas House, and Ted Cruz says Texas is blue. Elon Musk bet big on keeping it red. Here is what the wipeout means for his business empire, why Republicans in the state senate are reportedly moving against the new lieutenant governor, and what the fraud claims actually rest on.

hook.bold: Texas is blue. Ted Cruz said it himself. The richest man in the world bet on the other side, and now his business empire sits in a state that just voted against him.

descs.t: The Mississippi US Senate race between Democrat Scott Colom and Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith is still uncalled, with Colom ahead by about 2,000 votes and more than 95 percent reported. Mississippi has no automatic recount, and voters who cast affidavit ballots have until Tuesday, November 10 to fix them. This video walks through the count, the deadline and what comes next.

In a state Trump won by 25 points in 2024, Democrat Scott Colom leads Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith by about 2,000 votes, and posts point out that Hyde-Smith once blocked his confirmation as a federal judge. With Alaska also uncalled, Democrats would hold 56 Senate seats if they win both. This video looks at the numbers, the November 10 deadline and the fight over the ballots.

Mississippi's Senate race went from a 67 vote lead to about 2,000 votes in a day, and it is still not called. Scott Colom is ahead of Cindy Hyde-Smith, an independent says he drew votes from her, and affidavit voters have until November 10 to make their ballots count. This video lays out what could still change and why every remaining ballot matters.

intro.plain: Mississippi's Senate race still has no winner. Democrat Scott Colom leads Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith by about 2,000 votes with more than 95 percent counted, and Mississippi has no automatic recount. Voters who cast affidavit ballots have until Tuesday, November 10 to fix them. Chat, do you think this lead holds?

intro.bold: A lead of 67 votes in Mississippi turned into about 2,000. Scott Colom is ahead of Cindy Hyde-Smith, an independent says he pulled votes from her, and affidavit voters have until November 10 to make their ballots count. This race is not over. Chat, should every news desk wait, or call it now?

hook.bold: Sixty seven votes became about 2,000 in a single day. Mississippi's Senate seat is still up for grabs, and the ballots still out could decide it.

descs.t: Ilhan Omar has won a fifth term in Congress and addressed her victory party in Somali, and posts say nine more Somali Americans were elected to state legislatures in Minnesota, Ohio and Oregon. Critics called it an Islamic takeover; supporters called the attacks a racist smear. This video walks through who won and why the reaction got so heated.

Ilhan Omar's fifth term victory speech in Somali, and Abdul El-Sayed's in Arabic, set off a fight over language, loyalty and identity. One side calls it the Islamification of America, the other calls the backlash racist. This video looks past both slogans to what Omar has actually voted for and what it means for policy.

Ilhan Omar won again, and the argument about her has become a fight over her ancestry and her language. That is the wrong fight. This video makes the case for judging every politician by votes and ideas, never by group, and puts Omar's record where the debate should have started.

intro.plain: Ilhan Omar has won a fifth term in Congress, and she spoke to her victory party in Somali. Posts say nine more Somali Americans won state legislative seats in Minnesota, Ohio and Oregon. descs.t: Vice President JD Vance blamed the war with the Islamic Republic for the Republican midterm losses, as President Trump weighs his next move against the regime. Some officials push for new strikes while others want to wind down operations. We walk through what Vance said, what Trump said back, and how the regime responded.

JD Vance says the war with the Islamic Republic cost Republicans the midterms, while President Trump says it was worth it and the regime can never have a nuclear weapon. Reports say Vance is building a new right coalition ahead of 2028. We look at the split inside the administration and what it means for the next move.

Crowds in Tehran burned banners of Trump and Vance after the Republican midterm losses, and the regime's leaders claimed a political win. Now JD Vance blames the war itself for the defeat. We make the case for why one election should not decide whether America stops pressure on the Islamic Republic.

intro.plain: JD Vance is blaming the war with the Islamic Republic for the Republican midterm losses, and President Trump is weighing his next move against the regime. Some officials want new strikes, others want to wind down. Trump says the war was worth losing the midterms. So tell me in the chat: should one election change the plan?
intro.mid: The midterm blame game has a target, and it is the war. Vance says it cost Republicans the election. Trump says it was worth it, because the regime can never have a nuclear weapon. And reports say Vance is already building a new right for 2028. Chat, who has this right, Vance or Trump?
intro.bold: In Tehran they burned banners of Trump and Vance and danced in the streets. The regime's speaker mocked Vance. Khamenei says nothing changes. And now the Vice President is blaming the war for the midterm loss. If America walks away now, who really won? Tell me in the chat: hold the line or wind it down?
